subjects.name: Titanic
clues: Its director dived to a real shipwreck many times while researching this 1997 film.
A huge replica ship was built beside a giant water tank on the coast of Mexico.
It won 11 Oscars, tying the record set by Ben-Hur.
Celine Dion sang its theme song, 'My Heart Will Go On'.
Jack and Rose fall in love aboard a doomed ocean liner in 1912.
subjects.fact: It was the first film to earn more than one billion dollars worldwide.

subjects.name: Star Wars
clues: Much of this 1977 film's desert planet was filmed in Tunisia.
Studios doubted it, but it became the highest-grossing film of its time.
John Williams wrote its famous orchestral score, which won an Oscar.
A farm boy, a princess and a smuggler battle an evil Empire and its Death Star.
Luke Skywalker learns about the Force and faces Darth Vader.
subjects.fact: Its toys sold so fast that some fans got only an IOU certificate for Christmas 1977.

subjects.name: The Godfather
clues: This 1972 film was adapted from a bestselling novel by Mario Puzo.
Its music, including a haunting love theme, was composed by Nino Rota.
It won Best Picture, and so did its sequel two years later.
Al Pacino plays a war hero drawn into his family's business.
Marlon Brando plays Don Vito Corleone, head of a New York crime family.
subjects.fact: It was directed by Francis Ford Coppola, then only 32 years old.

subjects.name: Citizen Kane
clues: This 1941 film was made by a first-time film director aged just 25 when filming began.
Its deep-focus camerawork, sharp from front to back, was groundbreaking.
A newspaper tycoon who resembled its main character tried to stop its release.
Sight and Sound critics' polls ranked it the greatest film ever from 1962 to 2002.
Orson Welles plays a newspaper owner whose dying word is 'Rosebud'.
subjects.fact: Its only Oscar win was for Best Original Screenplay.

subjects.name: Jurassic Park
clues: This 1993 film was based on a novel by Michael Crichton.
It mixed groundbreaking computer-generated creatures with life-size animatronic models.
Scientists recreate extinct animals using DNA from mosquitoes trapped in amber.
A T. rex chases a jeep, and raptors stalk two children in a kitchen.
Steven Spielberg's dinosaur theme park adventure on an island near Costa Rica.
subjects.fact: It became the highest-grossing film of all time until Titanic overtook it.

subjects.name: Forrest Gump
clues: This 1994 film won six Oscars, including Best Picture.
Its hero meets several US presidents, cleverly inserted into real news footage.
He runs back and forth across America for over three years.
He becomes a shrimp boat captain and a ping-pong champion.
Tom Hanks plays a kind Alabama man who says life is like a box of chocolates.
subjects.fact: A real seafood restaurant chain, Bubba Gump Shrimp Company, was named after it.

subjects.name: The Matrix
clues: This 1999 science fiction film was written and directed by the Wachowskis.
It made 'bullet time' slow-motion camera effects famous.
Humans are unknowingly living in a computer simulation run by machines.
A hacker must choose between swallowing a red pill or a blue pill.
Keanu Reeves plays Neo, who learns kung fu in seconds and dodges bullets.
subjects.fact: It won all four Oscars it was nominated for, including Best Visual Effects.

subjects.name: Inception
clues: This 2010 film's hallway fight was filmed inside a giant rotating set.
Its score by Hans Zimmer is known for deep, booming horn blasts.
A team of thieves enters people's dreams to steal or plant ideas.
A small spinning top is used to check whether the hero is dreaming.
Christopher Nolan film in which Leonardo DiCaprio's dream city folds over itself.
subjects.fact: It won four Oscars, all for its technical work in sound, visual effects and cinematography.

subjects.name: Avatar
clues: This 2009 film was largely made with performance capture and shown in 3D.
It became the highest-grossing film of all time in early 2010.
Its story is set on Pandora, a lush moon of a giant planet.
A former marine who uses a wheelchair controls a tall alien body.
James Cameron's epic about the blue-skinned Na'vi people.
subjects.fact: Its director first planned the story in the 1990s but waited for effects technology to catch up.

subjects.name: Casablanca
clues: This 1942 film was released while World War II was raging and later won Best Picture.
It is set in a Moroccan city full of refugees trying to reach America.
Its song 'As Time Goes By' is played by the pianist Sam.
Humphrey Bogart plays Rick, a cafe owner who meets his old love Ilsa again.
It ends with a line about 'the beginning of a beautiful friendship'.
subjects.fact: It was filmed almost entirely on Hollywood studio sets, not in Africa.

subjects.name: Jaws
clues: This 1975 film was largely shot on the island of Martha's Vineyard.
Its mechanical star kept breaking down, so it is barely seen until late in the film.
Its simple two-note musical theme by John Williams signals danger.
A police chief, a scientist and a fisherman hunt a predator off a beach town.
Steven Spielberg's thriller about a giant great white shark.
subjects.fact: The film crew nicknamed the troublesome mechanical shark 'Bruce'.

subjects.name: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
clues: This 1982 film became the highest-grossing film of its time.
A boy hides a stranded visitor in his house, disguising it among his stuffed toys.
The visitor is lured with a trail of candy pieces.
Bicycles fly across the face of the moon in its most famous scene.
Steven Spielberg's film about a little alien who wants to 'phone home'.
subjects.fact: A young Drew Barrymore played the little sister, Gertie.

subjects.name: Seven Samurai
clues: This 1954 Japanese film runs for well over three hours.
Poor farmers hire wandering swordsmen to defend their village from bandits.
It was remade as a classic Hollywood western starring Yul Brynner in 1960.
Its final battle is fought in pouring rain and deep mud.
Akira Kurosawa's epic, starring Toshiro Mifune as a wild, would-be warrior.
subjects.fact: It is often credited with popularising the story of assembling a team for a mission.

subjects.name: Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge
clues: This 1995 Hindi film was the directing debut of Aditya Chopra.
Much of its first half takes place on a holiday trip across Europe.
It played at Mumbai's Maratha Mandir cinema for over 1,000 weeks.
In its finale the heroine runs to catch a departing train and her lover's hand.
Shah Rukh Khan and Kajol play Raj and Simran in this Bollywood romance.
subjects.fact: Its title means roughly 'The Big-Hearted Will Take the Bride'.

subjects.name: Sholay
clues: This 1975 Hindi film was shot among rocky hills near Bangalore.
A retired police officer hires two small-time crooks to catch a bandit.
Its villain Gabbar Singh became one of Bollywood's most famous baddies.
Two pals sing the friendship song 'Yeh Dosti' while riding a motorcycle.
Amitabh Bachchan and Dharmendra play Jai and Veeru in this action classic.
subjects.fact: Its title means 'Embers' in Hindi.

subjects.name: Parasite
clues: This 2019 South Korean film won the Palme d'Or at Cannes.
A poor family living in a semi-basement flat finds work with a rich family.
Its big twist involves a secret bunker below a stylish modern house.
It won four Oscars, including Best Director and Best Picture.
Bong Joon-ho's film, the first non-English language Best Picture winner.
subjects.fact: Its rich family's house was a set built specially for the film.

subjects.name: Back to the Future
clues: Steven Spielberg was an executive producer of this 1985 film.
Its teenage hero accidentally stops his own parents from meeting in 1955.
A lightning strike on a clock tower supplies the power he needs.
Its time machine must reach 88 miles per hour to work.
Michael J. Fox plays Marty McFly, who travels in time in a DeLorean car.
subjects.fact: It was the highest-grossing film of 1985 in the United States.

subjects.name: Raiders of the Lost Ark
clues: This 1981 adventure was a team-up between George Lucas and Steven Spielberg.
Its hero is a college professor of archaeology who hates snakes.
In the opening scene the hero outruns a giant rolling boulder.
Set in 1936, the hero races Nazi agents to find a sacred biblical chest.
Harrison Ford's first outing as Indiana Jones, with his whip and fedora.
subjects.fact: Tom Selleck was first choice for the hero but was tied up with the TV show Magnum, P.I.

subjects.name: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
clues: This 1937 film was Walt Disney's first full-length animated feature.
Doubters in Hollywood called it 'Disney's Folly' before it became a huge hit.
Its songs include 'Heigh-Ho' and 'Someday My Prince Will Come'.
A wicked queen asks her magic mirror who is the fairest of them all.
A princess bites a poisoned apple after hiding with a band of little miners.

links.name: Mickey Mouse
links.rel: came from the same studio as

subjects.fact: Walt Disney received an honorary Oscar for it: one full-size statuette and seven small ones.

subjects.name: The Lion King
clues: This 1994 Disney film's songs were written by Elton John and Tim Rice.
Its story borrows ideas from Shakespeare's Hamlet.
Its opening song, 'Circle of Life', presents a newborn prince on Pride Rock.
A meerkat and a warthog teach the young hero the motto 'Hakuna Matata'.
Young Simba must reclaim his place after his father Mufasa dies.
subjects.fact: 'Can You Feel the Love Tonight' from the film won the Oscar for Best Original Song.

subjects.name: Toy Story
clues: This 1995 film was the first feature film made entirely with computer animation.
It was the first feature film from Pixar.
Its song 'You've Got a Friend in Me' was written by Randy Newman.
A spaceman action figure believes he is a real space ranger.
Woody the cowboy and Buzz Lightyear compete for Andy's affection.
subjects.fact: Its director John Lasseter received a special Oscar for leading the project.

subjects.name: Spirited Away
clues: This 2001 film was Japan's highest-grossing film for almost two decades.
It shared the Golden Bear prize at the Berlin Film Festival.
A girl works in a bathhouse for gods after her parents are turned into pigs.
Its characters include the masked No-Face and the witch Yubaba.
Hayao Miyazaki's Oscar-winning tale of ten-year-old Chihiro.
subjects.fact: It was the first anime film to win the Oscar for Best Animated Feature.

subjects.name: Frozen
clues: This 2013 film was loosely inspired by Hans Christian Andersen's The Snow Queen.
It won Oscars for Best Animated Feature and Best Original Song.
A cheerful snowman named Olaf dreams of summer.
Princess Anna sets out to find her sister, who has icy magic powers.
Queen Elsa sings 'Let It Go' while building an ice palace.

links.name: Hans Christian Andersen
links.rel: is inspired by a tale by

subjects.fact: Its kingdom of Arendelle was inspired by the scenery and buildings of Norway.

subjects.name: Shrek
clues: This 2001 film won the first ever Oscar for Best Animated Feature.
It was made by DreamWorks and pokes fun at classic fairy tales.
A talking donkey tags along on a quest to rescue a princess.
Princess Fiona hides a secret that appears every night after sunset.
A grumpy green ogre who lives in a swamp, voiced by Mike Myers.
subjects.fact: It was based on a 1990 picture book by William Steig.

subjects.name: Finding Nemo
clues: This 2003 Pixar film won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature.
Much of it is set on the Great Barrier Reef and in Sydney Harbour.
A forgetful blue tang named Dory helps on a long journey.
Sea turtles ride the East Australian Current like a highway.
A worried clownfish father crosses the ocean to rescue his lost son.
subjects.fact: A sequel, Finding Dory, followed in 2016.

subjects.name: My Neighbor Totoro
clues: This 1988 film was first shown as a double bill with Grave of the Fireflies.
Two sisters move to the countryside while their mother is in hospital.
A giant grinning cat-shaped bus gives rides through the night.
Its big, furry main creature became the logo of Studio Ghibli.
Hayao Miyazaki's tale of a forest spirit who waits at a bus stop in the rain.
subjects.fact: It is set in the Japanese countryside in the 1950s.

subjects.name: The Simpsons
clues: This show began as short cartoons on The Tracey Ullman Show in 1987.
Its creator Matt Groening named most of the family after his own relatives.
In 2018 it passed Gunsmoke as America's longest-running scripted primetime series.
It is set in the town of Springfield, home to a nuclear power plant.
Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa and Maggie are a yellow-skinned cartoon family.
subjects.fact: A feature film based on the show was released in 2007.

subjects.name: Friends
clues: This sitcom ran for ten seasons, from 1994 to 2004.
Its theme song 'I'll Be There for You' was performed by The Rembrandts.
Its six main stars each earned a million dollars per episode in its last seasons.
Most scenes take place in two apartments or the Central Perk coffee shop.
Six pals in New York: Rachel, Ross, Monica, Chandler, Joey and Phoebe.
subjects.fact: Rachel's layered haircut, nicknamed 'The Rachel', became a 1990s craze.

subjects.name: Doctor Who
clues: This BBC science fiction series first aired on 23 November 1963.
When its first lead actor became ill, the hero was allowed to 'regenerate' into a new face.
Its villains include the robotic Daleks and the Cybermen.
Its time machine looks like a blue police box and is bigger on the inside.
A time-travelling alien from Gallifrey flies the TARDIS with human companions.
subjects.fact: Its eerie electronic theme tune was realised by Delia Derbyshire in 1963.

subjects.name: Sesame Street
clues: This children's TV show first aired in the United States in 1969.
It was designed with researchers to help young children learn letters and numbers.
Its characters include Big Bird, Elmo and Oscar the Grouch.
Each episode is 'brought to you' by a letter and a number of the day.
Jim Henson's Muppets Bert, Ernie and Cookie Monster live here.
subjects.fact: Versions of the show have been made for children in many countries around the world.

subjects.name: Stranger Things
clues: This show's first season was released on Netflix in 2016.
Set in 1980s Indiana, it celebrates the films and music of that decade.
Kids on bikes play Dungeons & Dragons and name a monster after a creature from it.
A girl called Eleven, who has special powers, loves Eggo waffles.
A group of kids search the 'Upside Down' for their missing pal Will Byers.
subjects.fact: It was created by twin brothers Matt and Ross Duffer.

subjects.name: Star Trek
clues: This science fiction show first aired in 1966 and lasted only three seasons at first.
Fan letter campaigns helped keep it alive, and it later grew into many films and series.
Its crew carries communicators and phasers and is 'beamed' by a transporter.
The logical, pointy-eared Mr. Spock serves as science officer.
Captain Kirk commands the starship Enterprise, boldly going where no one has gone before.
subjects.fact: NASA named its first space shuttle test orbiter Enterprise after fans wrote in.

subjects.name: Seinfeld
clues: This sitcom first aired in 1989 and ran for nine seasons.
It was co-created by comedian Larry David.
It has often been described as 'a show about nothing'.
Its characters include George, Elaine and the wacky neighbour Kramer.
A stand-up comedian named Jerry and his pals get into everyday scrapes in New York.
subjects.fact: Its final episode in 1998 was watched by about 76 million viewers in the United States.

subjects.name: Mr. Bean
clues: This British comedy first aired on 1 January 1990.
Its hero hardly speaks, so it is enjoyed by viewers all over the world.
He drives a lime-green Mini and talks to his teddy bear.
It led to two feature films and an animated cartoon series.
Rowan Atkinson plays the bumbling, nearly silent title character.
subjects.fact: Its title character often locks his car with a padlock and bolt.

subjects.name: Planet Earth
clues: This 2006 BBC nature series was one of the first filmed in high definition.
Its crews used stabilised cameras on helicopters to film wolves hunting from far above.
Its episodes visited deserts, oceans, jungles, caves and polar ice.
A 2016 sequel became famous for a chase between baby iguanas and racer snakes.
David Attenborough narrated this sweeping tour of the world's habitats.
subjects.fact: It took about five years to make.

subjects.name: Super Mario Bros.
clues: This 1985 game was bundled with the Nintendo Entertainment System in North America.
It was designed by Shigeru Miyamoto and Takashi Tezuka.
Its hero grows bigger by eating mushrooms and travels through green pipes.
Its catchy theme music was composed by Koji Kondo.
A plumber stomps on Goombas on his way to rescue a princess from Bowser.
subjects.fact: For decades it was one of the best-selling video games ever made.

subjects.name: Tetris
clues: This puzzle game was created in Moscow in 1984.
Its creator, Alexey Pajitnov, worked at a Soviet computer research centre.
It became a huge hit when bundled with the Game Boy in 1989.
Each of its seven pieces is made of four squares.
Players rotate falling blocks to fill and clear horizontal lines.
subjects.fact: Its theme is based on the Russian folk song 'Korobeiniki'.

subjects.name: Pac-Man
clues: This 1980 arcade game was designed by Toru Iwatani in Japan.
Its creator said the hero's shape was inspired by a pizza with a slice missing.
Four ghosts named Blinky, Pinky, Inky and Clyde chase the player.
Eating a power pellet lets the hero gobble up the ghosts for points.
A yellow circle with a big mouth munches dots through a maze.
subjects.fact: A perfect score of 3,333,360 points was first achieved in 1999.

subjects.name: Minecraft
clues: This game was created by the Swedish programmer Markus Persson.
Microsoft bought its studio, Mojang, in 2014.
By 2023 it had sold over 300 million copies, more than any other video game.
Players fight off green Creepers that sneak up and explode.
A blocky world where players dig for resources and build anything they imagine.
subjects.fact: Its full version was released in November 2011, after a popular early test version.

subjects.name: Pong
clues: This 1972 arcade game was one of the first big video game hits.
It was released by Atari, the company founded by Nolan Bushnell.
Its designer Allan Alcorn made it as a training exercise.
Its first test machine stopped working because it was stuffed with coins.
Two paddles bounce a square ball back and forth in this simple table tennis game.
subjects.fact: Its test machine was placed in a California bar called Andy Capp's Tavern.

subjects.name: The Legend of Zelda
clues: This 1986 Nintendo game came on a gold cartridge in North America that could save progress.
Its designer based it on his boyhood explorations of caves and forests.
An old man in a cave hands the hero a sword, saying 'It's dangerous to go alone!'
Players collect pieces of the Triforce in the land of Hyrule.
Link, a green-clad young hero, battles Ganon to save a princess.
subjects.fact: Its hero is named Link, and the princess is the one in the title.

subjects.name: Space Invaders
clues: This 1978 arcade game was designed by Tomohiro Nishikado for Taito.
Its enemies speed up as their numbers shrink, partly because the hardware runs faster.
Players hide behind crumbling shields while dodging falling shots.
A mystery saucer flies across the top of the screen for bonus points.
Rows of pixel aliens march down toward a laser cannon at the bottom.
subjects.fact: It helped start the golden age of arcade video games.

subjects.name: Fortnite
clues: This game launched in 2017, made by Epic Games.
Its free Battle Royale mode drops 100 players onto an island.
Players build ramps and walls in seconds during battles.
It has hosted huge in-game concerts, including one by Marshmello in 2019.
A shrinking storm forces players together in this colourful last-player-standing game.
subjects.fact: Its victory dances, called emotes, spread into playgrounds around the world.

subjects.name: Angry Birds
clues: This 2009 mobile game was made by the company Rovio in Finland.
It became one of the most popular paid apps of the early smartphone era.
Players pull back a slingshot by dragging a finger on the screen.
Its heroes want revenge on green pigs that stole their eggs.
Players fling round, cross-looking feathered heroes at towers built by pigs.
subjects.fact: It inspired an animated feature film in 2016.

subjects.name: Mickey Mouse
clues: He became famous in the 1928 sound cartoon Steamboat Willie.
Walt Disney himself provided his voice for many years.
He wears red shorts, big yellow shoes and white gloves.
His girlfriend Minnie and his dog Pluto often appear alongside him.
This cheerful cartoon rodent with round black ears is Disney's mascot.
subjects.fact: He received an honorary star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 1978, his 50th birthday.

subjects.name: Darth Vader
clues: He first appeared in a 1977 film, wearing a black helmet and cape.
He was played in costume by the bodybuilder David Prowse.
James Earl Jones provided his deep voice.
His heavy mechanical breathing became one of film's most famous sounds.
A Sith Lord who reveals to Luke Skywalker, 'I am your father'.
subjects.fact: His real name before he turned to the dark side was Anakin Skywalker.

subjects.name: Mario
clues: He first appeared in 1981 in Donkey Kong, where he was called Jumpman.
He was given a moustache because a mouth was hard to draw with so few pixels.
His taller brother Luigi dresses in green.
His enemy Bowser keeps kidnapping Princess Peach.
Nintendo's famous plumber wears a red cap with an 'M' on it.
subjects.fact: He was created by Shigeru Miyamoto.

subjects.name: Pikachu
clues: He first appeared in 1996 in Japanese video games for the Game Boy.
His name mixes Japanese sounds for a sparkle and a mouse's squeak.
In the cartoon he refuses to go in his ball and rides on Ash's shoulder.
His red cheeks store electricity, which he releases in Thunderbolt attacks.
This yellow electric mouse is the most famous Pokémon of all.
subjects.fact: A Japanese airline once painted Pikachu-themed jumbo jets.

subjects.name: Homer Simpson
clues: He first appeared in 1987 in short cartoons on a TV variety show.
He is voiced by Dan Castellaneta.
He works as a safety inspector at a nuclear power plant.
He loves doughnuts and lives at 742 Evergreen Terrace.
Bald, lazy and lovable, he shouts 'D'oh!' and is Bart's dad.
subjects.fact: His catchphrase 'D'oh!' was added to the Oxford English Dictionary in 2001.

subjects.name: Bugs Bunny
clues: He made his official debut in the 1940 cartoon A Wild Hare.
Mel Blanc gave him his famous Brooklyn-style voice.
He often outwits the hunter Elmer Fudd.
He received his own star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame in 1985.
This Looney Tunes rabbit munches a carrot and asks 'Eh, what's up, Doc?'
subjects.fact: He shared a scene with Mickey Mouse in the 1988 film Who Framed Roger Rabbit.

subjects.name: SpongeBob SquarePants
clues: His TV show first aired in 1999, created by a former marine biology teacher.
He works as a fry cook at the Krusty Krab.
His best buddy is a pink starfish named Patrick.
He lives in a pineapple under the sea in Bikini Bottom.
This cheerful yellow sea sponge wears square brown trousers.
subjects.fact: His creator was Stephen Hillenburg.

subjects.name: Sonic the Hedgehog
clues: He first appeared in a 1991 video game for the Sega Mega Drive.
He was created to give Sega a mascot to rival Nintendo's star plumber.
He collects golden rings and drops them when he gets hit.
His sidekick is a two-tailed fox named Tails.
Sega's super-fast blue hero curls into a spinning ball to attack.
subjects.fact: His first live-action feature film was released in 2020.
